provider: Kaggle dataset quota-request program (the >200 GB escape hatch)

free_tier.stated: Not a fixed number: Kaggle staff grant additional per-dataset storage quota on request via a short Google Form, explicitly to 'host large, important public datasets'. This is the documented path past the 200 GB per-dataset ceiling.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Same free GCS-backed delivery as any other public dataset.

tooling: Same as Kaggle Datasets. The request form is forms.gle/jh4uBjtP7CsfH97C9 (linked from the staff post).
chaining: This is what turns 200 GB/dataset into multi-TB single objects. Kaggle's own advice is to shard by meaningful subset, which is exactly the sharding pattern the workload needs anyway. Combine: N shards x 200 GB each (no request needed) OR one request for a multi-TB dataset.
